R983.note: preg_replace_callback + allowlist closes /e code execution; allowlist includes the case's own default formatter (strtoupper), so default behavior is preserved.

R986.note: Standard parameterized query replacing Sprintf concatenation; correct and behavior-preserving.

R989.note: Captures bytesSent() immediately after send(), before the conditional reset; return value is identical to before since nothing else mutates bytesSent_ in between.

R990.note: Sign-checked, underflow-safe reordering of the bounds check closes the wraparound while accepting exactly the same valid windows as the original check.

R992.note: Replaces eval with a 4-strategy lookup, but the case shows admins author free-form expressions (e.g. 'basePrice * (quantity>10?0.9:1.0)'); no existing formula matches the 4 hardcoded keys, so every existing product's pricing rule now silently falls back to basePrice with no error, while the write-up incorrectly claims 'the external contract... remains unchanged.'

R993.note: Encode.forHtml() applied to the Referer value used as the format string; obj args and Locale-based formatting call are otherwise unchanged.

R995.note: JSON.parse + ajv schema correctly eliminates node-serialize's eval-based RCE; the resulting cookie-format break for existing sessions is explicitly disclosed as a required migration.

R996.note: RandomNumberGenerator.Fill + hex string is the correct CSPRNG replacement; token remains an opaque string used identically in the dictionary and response.

R997.note: Standard SqlParameter/@ownerName fix; behavior otherwise unchanged.

R998.note: snprintf with an explicit truncation/error check rejects oversized entries rather than corrupting the buffer; reasonable and clearly disclosed choice given no stated contract.

R999.note: SafeUnpickler's whitelist only allows the top-level Model/RandomForest* classes, but a pickled sklearn estimator's state pulls in numpy internals (e.g. numpy.core.multiarray._reconstruct) that find_class would also reject, so real cached models likely fail to deserialize at all — an undisclosed break of 'returns a prediction for an existing model'. The HMAC key is also a hardcoded literal shared by producer and consumer, so anyone who can read the source can forge a valid signature, undermining the integrity check that is the fix's other pillar.

R1000.note: Removing the attacker-controlled env array entirely is correct since it served no legitimate purpose; the echo command still runs with the default environment.
